en: The *Śakrapraśnasūtra*... [the Buddha] was dwelling among the Magadhans, as before, up to [his stay] in the rock cave. "Come, let us go and attend upon him.
"It is most auspicious for you, Kauśika," said Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas, to Śakra, the lord of the gods.

Having given his word, he took a lute with a lapis lazuli handle upon his shoulder and approached to serve Śakra, the lord of the gods; the other gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three also heard of this. Śakra, the lord of the gods, and Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas, prepared themselves to go before the Blessed One to see him and to attend upon him; thereupon they too made their preparations.
To show themselves to the Blessed One and to attend upon the Blessed One,

Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas— just as a strong man might extend his bent arm or bend his extended arm— in that very same way, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and Pañcaśikha...

And the Gandharva-son... the Trāyastriṃśa gods vanished among the Trāyastriṃśa gods... not far from Mount Vaidehaka. At that time, O Vaidehaka... as if an intense radiance had arisen like fire... indeed on Mount Vaidehaka. ... Alas, Mount Vaidehaka is being consumed by fire... Mount Vaidehaka.

Indeed, O Vaidehaka... Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, [addressed] Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas... "Those forms, dear Pañcaśikha, that Blessed One [frequented] in the wilderness and forests... devoid of human settlements... were frequented and suitable for solitary retreat. If, then..."
"O Mahāśakya, Mahāśakya... it is not easy to approach [him] in the same way as one has not previously experienced [him].
If you, dear Pañcaśikha... were to approach the Blessed One for a vision, that would be most auspicious for you, Kauśika. Thus spoke Pañcaśikha...
Knowing that he would hear the sound of his speech without being too close,
[he took] a lute with a lapis lazuli handle...
and spoke a verse associated with the state of an Arhat.
I pay homage to your father, O auspicious one,
Tumburu, who possesses the splendor of the sun...
The Sakyan son, unified in meditation, alert and mindful, seeks the deathless as a sage.
I spoke thus to Sūryavarcas.
Just as a sage would rejoice upon attaining supreme enlightenment, so too,
O virtuous lady, should you rejoice.
He attained the state of a woman because of her.
Just as medicine for the sick or food for the hungry,
bring about final Nibbāna, O Bhaddā.
Like water with water.
If Sakka, the lord of the Thirty-three, were to grant me a boon,
I would choose you, O Bhaddā, as my boon.
In this way, desire is firm for me.
O wise one, I pay homage and revere you, my father, like a *sāla* tree in full bloom.
For whom there is such a person as this.
… the encounter with Mātali’s charioteer … that very meeting, O Venerable One, was for me [like] being with that Blessed One …
"...there was earth... beyond that, I do not recall.
Then this thought occurred to Śakra, the lord of the gods: 'The Blessed One is conversing with Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas; the Blessed One... "
He said this: ...
[saying] in our name...
[asking after] your freedom from illness and your ease of movement.
"May there be supreme good fortune for you, O Kauśika! Having thus replied to Śakra, the Lord of the Devas, Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas, approached the Blessed One.
Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and stood to one side.
Standing to one side...
… therein indeed is dispassion … and the danger in sensual pleasures … //
…these yokes of Māra, which are difficult to transcend,
O Noble One…
... [he spoke] regarding the hosts of gods.
The gods, together with Indra, and [the others] ... in the assembly hall;
the two of them gazed upon [them] equally ... //
Having sent them forth, Śakra, the lord of the gods, experienced a surge of agitation;
[the two] were reborn in the body [of Brahmā].
He transcends the Heaven of the Thirty-three. … Gopaka addressed Vāsava:
"The Buddha, the Victor…"
… they say, "Desire."
These are his sons, [whose] memory...
/ ...of them...
/ delusion is other; because of various...

...the element ... and the world. Indeed, therefore, sentient beings, perceiving this very element, grasp it firmly, adhere to it, and engage in conventional discourse regarding it: "This alone is the truth; all else is delusion. "It is so, worthy sir! It is so, worthy sir! Yet indeed, not all sentient beings have the same desires or the same inclinations, as previously stated, up until:
"This alone is the truth; all else is delusion.
And having understood this meaning from the presence of the Blessed One, [he said:]
As before, up to: “… here … or you.
But, friend, are all those ascetics and brahmins completely successful, completely stainless, and have they reached the ultimate consummation of the holy life?”
"Indeed not, Kauśika! Not all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas have reached the ultimate goal, are ultimately stainless, and have reached the ultimate consummation of the holy life.
Why is it, Kauśika, that not all śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas have reached the ultimate goal, are ultimately stainless, and have reached the ultimate consummation of the holy life?
Rather, only those few śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas who have attained liberation through the total exhaustion of craving..."
… … in all the worlds there is no person who is your equal.
I pay homage to you, O Great Hero;
I pay homage to you, O Supreme Person,
the destroyer of the thorn of craving.
The Buddha, the kinsman of the sun.
"Do you recall, Kauśika, whether previously another such attainment of seclusion and attainment of joy has ever arisen? "I do recall it, Blessed One.
Once in the past, when the gods and the asuras were at war... the gods were victorious and the asuras were defeated..."

“… Venerable sir, this occurred to me: ‘Whether it be celestial vitality or the vitality of the asuras, we shall consume both of them together. Yet that attainment of joy and attainment of seclusion of mine has resulted in quarreling, resulted in brawling, resulted in strife, and resulted in dispute.”
"This attainment of joy and attainment of seclusion of mine— which culminates in no quarreling, no brawling, no strife, and no dispute— is [attained] in the presence of the Blessed One.
But from where does this clarity arise?"

Then, venerable sir, this thought occurred to me: "Having passed away from here, I shall be reborn among the nature of human beings; there, I shall be born into those families that are wealthy, possessing great riches and great enjoyments, with abundant wealth and resources, abundant property and assets, abundant stores of gold, grain, treasuries, and granaries, and having many friends, ministers, kinsmen, and blood relations, as well as many female and male slaves, laborers, and servants."

Having been born into such families by nature, and having grown through lineage and the maturation of the faculties, I shall shave off my hair and beard, don saffron robes, and go forth from the home to the homeless state with perfect faith. Thus, O Venerable One, as I practice in accordance with the Dharma, may I proceed.
If there will be full knowledge,
we shall become those who have fully known;
this indeed is the end of suffering.
If, as I practice according to the right method, there should be no higher knowledge for me...
those gods who are material, mind-made, unimpaired, with all faculties intact, complete in all limbs and minor members, and abiding in a beautiful complexion.
Feeding on joy, taking joy as their sustenance, self-luminous, traveling through the air, long-lived, and long-enduring— such will be my rebirth. Having passed away from those divine bodies,
I shall enter a womb.
...the mind will find delight.
upright ...
practicing the alms-round ...
Devoted to the holy life.
If, as I practice according to the right method, there shall be full understanding,
we shall become those who have understood.
This indeed is the end of suffering.
"Venerable sir, as I practice according to the Dhamma, if there should be no further instruction for me,
then may those deities who have long lifespans [grant it]."
These have been heard as the finality;
for in the end, when [the world] is decaying,
that will be the dwelling place.
“I am a stream-enterer, Blessed One; I am a stream-enterer, Tathāgata. [The fruit] has been attained... for the sake of once-returning... [O] Kauśika, what...”
Va au … taṁ pra … sa … ulamadhyāgā…r … Śakra replied:
"Where the Blessed One … ṣ … nno."
Nowhere else, nor anywhere else,
has such a thing been seen before.
"… by me, having become a god while seated, O worthy one, life was obtained once again."
In this way, the perception of refuge...

While this Dharma-discourse was being spoken, the dust-free, stainless eye of Dharma regarding all phenomena arose in Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and in eighty thousand deities. Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, having seen the Dharma, attained the Dharma, known the Dharma, and plunged deeply into the Dharma— having crossed over doubt, transcended perplexity, becoming independent of others and not led by another— attained confidence regarding the teachings within the Teacher’s instruction.

Rising from his seat, draping his upper robe over one shoulder, and bowing with palms joined toward the Blessed One, he said this to the Blessed One: "I have come for refuge, Venerable Sir; I have come for refuge. I go for refuge to the Blessed One, to the Dharma, and to the Saṅgha of monks. May the Blessed One accept me as a lay follower from this day forward, for as long as life lasts, one who has taken refuge and is filled with faith."

Then Śakra, the lord of the gods, addressed Pañcaśikha, the son of the Gandharvas: "You have been helpful to us, dear Pañcaśikha; indeed, you have been most helpful to us in that you [have praised] the Blessed One."
